description: Environment and health around the Kolwezi mines: the 2025-2026 scientific evidence base
verification_status: confirmed by a primary source - four independent scientific studies, published by RAID/AFREWATCH/Source International in June 2026

2026_study.coverage: 8 communities around Kolwezi and Fungurume, Lualaba province
2026_study.testimony: over 150 interviews with residents and medical staff
2026_study.sampling: 12 surface-water samples and 9 sediment samples (October 2025), plus 5 wells
2026_study.air_findings: fine particulate matter exceeded WHO limits by wide margins at EVERY measurement point; researchers called it among the worst readings recorded at mining sites worldwide over years of monitoring; the first independent PM measurement in the region
2026_study.water_and_sediment_findings: elevated concentrations of copper, cobalt, manganese, arsenic, lead, and uranium; copper was the most critical pollutant, exceeding several international standards; metal concentrations in the Kelangile River and Lake Kando above international norms
2026_study.critical_case_well: a community well in Kolwezi, 200m from a tailings dam, was 100 times more acidic than recommended, with manganese and aluminum up to 14 times above health limits (manganese at these levels is neurotoxic)
2026_study.critical_case_school: Galaxy school in Kolwezi, under 500m from COMMUS's waste pile, showed some of the highest air-pollution readings in the study; children spend hours there daily
2026_study.resident_complaints: constant dust (households wash floors 3-4 times a day), falling crop yields, shrinking fish stocks, coughing, headaches, nosebleeds, skin and eye irritation

corporate_responses.Glencore (MUMI): a brief response acknowledging the findings and pledging to factor them into environmental management systems
corporate_responses.COMMUS (Zijin): requested an extension after the 1 June deadline; a later comment attributed Kolwezi's pollution partly to natural geological background and historic mining, and cited ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certification

prior_studies.raid_afrewatch_2024: the 'Beneath the Green' report (110 pages) - five mines (TFM/CMOC, Metalkol/ERG, COMMUS/Zijin, KCC, and MUMI/Glencore) together supply two-fifths of world cobalt; Kolwezi (population 500,000+) is described as an emerging 'sacrifice zone'
prior_studies.reproductive_health: journalistic investigation (Mongabay, 2024-2025) in Musonoi, near the COMMUS pit: a nurse at the 'La Trinite' clinic reports 5-10 reproductive-health cases a month (~100/year), with documented birth defects
prior_studies.2018_biomonitoring: a Kolwezi study (PubMed) found residents of a district turned into an artisanal cobalt pit had significantly higher urinary and blood cobalt levels than a control area, most pronounced in children, who also showed signs of oxidative DNA damage

commus_profile.owners: Zijin Mining 72% (some sources say 67%), Gecamines 28%, DRC 5%
commus_profile.location: under 2 km from central Kolwezi, homes within 500m of the pit
commus_profile.2023_production: 129,000 t of copper and cobalt (per Zijin's own data)
commus_profile.note: this asset was absent from the user's original documents - a significant gap, as it is one of the country's largest Chinese-linked mines

deforestation: AFREWATCH published (March 2026) a separate deforestation assessment for Lualaba and Haut-Katanga provinces
